page: The Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside instruction set support for AVX-512 (including AVX512_VNNI and AVX512_BF16) and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Resource allocation combines 32.0 GB of system memory (8.0 GB per core) with 400 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. There are no discrete hardware accelerators included, with GPU count standing at 0.0. Network capabilities feature 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. The generous 8:1 memory-to-core ratio positions this server in a memory-optimized footprint, complemented by high-speed local disk capacity.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, with stress-ng single-core achieving a top-tier score of 3432.87 and Geekbench single-core reaching a strong score of 2146.0. Memory throughput is also solid, recording 112.99 GB/sec on uncached large-block writes and a strong PassMark memory score of 2834.0. Single-threaded compression benchmarks such as gzip (32.3 GB/sec) and bzip3 (14.56 GB/sec) test strongly. Conversely, multithreaded capacity is constrained by the 4-vCPU envelope, resulting in mid-tier PassMark CPU (11732.08) and Geekbench multi-core (6741.0) figures, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput land in the lower quartiles.

Given its high memory allocation per core and dedicated CPU execution, this instance provides efficient resource density for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, moderate memory-intensive backend services, build automation, and ETL operations that require rapid local disk scratch space and high per-thread responsiveness without requiring large core counts.
description: The Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores at 2.0 GHz) and 32.0 GB of RAM. Bundled with 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and lacking a discrete GPU, it delivers an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Single-core compute capability is prominent, demonstrated by a top-tier stress-ng single-core score of 3432.87 and strong Geekbench single-core results, supported by AVX-512 instruction extensions. Memory bandwidth is equally competent, reflecting strong large-block write performance. Multi-core and high-concurrency throughput are naturally limited by the physical core count, making this configuration well matched for memory-heavy utilities, caching systems like Redis, single-threaded processing pipelines, and light database workloads requiring fast local NVMe storage.
